text.p: Workers at Venezuelan telephone company CANTV began an indefinite strike Thursday, but talks with management to reach a wage accord will continue, union representatives said.

"We've begun the national strike and we'll continue until we reach an agreement with the company," Audio Rincon, secretary general of the umbrella telecommunications union group Fetratel, told Reuters.
Rincon said union members would meet with management at the Labor Ministry at 1500 local time/1400 EST to resume discussions over wage contracts for 1997 and 1998.

Workers are now aiming for a 140 percent pay rise, spread over two years, down from a previous demand for an 154 percent increase. Rincon said the company had so far offered a 23 percent rise this year and another 20 percent increase in 1998.
A CANTV spokesman would not confirm that was the company's offer, but said a new wages contract proposal would be presented this afternoon.
"The idea is that the strike, whose effects have been minimal due to a small turn-out, end as soon as possible," said the source, who declined to be identified.
Of the company's 17,300 employees, around 6,200 are unionized.
CANTV said late Wednesday it has put in place mechanisms that would ensure continued service to all its clients while the strike continued.
CANTV share prices recovered Thursday morning after sliding some 15 percent over the past two weeks on concern over the strike and possible delays in rate increases.
CANTV traded up 145 bolivars at 1,990 in Caracas, while its American Depository Receipts were up 2 at 29-1/4 by 1137 local time/1037 EST on Wall Street.
